    • initializeCycle

      public Cycle initializeCycle(AppState state, double totalAllowance, LocalDate startDate, LocalDate endDate)
      Creates the first active budget cycle for US #1 and saves it immediately.

      Validation rules: allowance must be greater than zero, and end date must be strictly after start date.

      Parameters:
      state - application state to update
      totalAllowance - user's starting cash allowance
      startDate - cycle start date
      endDate - cycle end date
      Returns:
      the newly created active cycle

    • initializeCycle

    • calculateInitialSafeDailyLimit

      public double calculateInitialSafeDailyLimit(Cycle cycle)
      Calculates the initial safe daily limit for a new cycle.

      Formula: totalAllowance / numberOfDays. The number of days is the calendar-day distance from start date to end date, so 2026-05-05 to 2026-06-04 is 30 days.

      Parameters:
      cycle - active budget cycle
      Returns:
      initial safe daily limit

    • calculateRemainingBalance

      public double calculateRemainingBalance(AppState state)

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      remaining cycle balance

    • calculateSafeDailyLimit

      public double calculateSafeDailyLimit(AppState state, LocalDate today)
      Calculates safe daily limit for the current date using remaining balance and remaining days.

      Formula: remainingBalance / remainingDays. If the date is on or after the end date, this method uses one remaining day so the dashboard can still show a final-day amount.

      Parameters:
      state - application state containing active cycle and expenses
      today - current date used for the calculation
      Returns:
      safe daily limit for today

    • handleRolloverIfNeeded

      public CycleManager.RolloverResult handleRolloverIfNeeded(AppState state, LocalDate today)
      Handles US #5 rollover when the app starts or the dashboard opens.

      No background scheduler is used. If today is after the cycle's lastCalculatedDate, this method updates that date, saves JSON immediately, and returns the recalculated balance, remaining days, and safe daily limit. Unspent money naturally rolls into the new limit because the formula uses current remaining balance over current remaining days.

      Parameters:
      state - application state containing the active cycle and expenses
      today - current date used for rollover detection
      Returns:
      rollover calculation result for the UI to display

    • checkThresholds

      public CycleManager.ThresholdResult checkThresholds(AppState state)
      Checks spending thresholds for the active cycle (US #6).

      Rules:

      • If spent >= allowance → budget exhausted.
      • If spent/allowance >= 0.80 and the warning has not been shown before → show warning once and persist the flag.

      This method may save JSON if it needs to mark the 80% warning as shown.

      Parameters:
      state - application state containing active cycle and expenses
      Returns:
      threshold result for the UI

    • resetCycle

      public void resetCycle(AppState state, double newAllowance, String startDate, String endDate)
      Resets the current budget cycle (US #11). Jana

      Clears all expenses and creates a new cycle with the given allowance and dates. Changes are saved immediately.

      Parameters:
      state - application state
      newAllowance - new cycle allowance
      startDate - start date (yyyy-MM-dd)
      endDate - end date (yyyy-MM-dd)

    • resetCycle

      public void resetCycle(AppState state)
      Resets the current budget cycle (US #11).

      Clears the active cycle and removes all expenses. Categories and privacy settings are kept. Changes are saved immediately.

      Parameters:
      state - application state to update
